issues: Core result reproduces exactly and the control is non-vacuous (zero-spread stochastic == deterministic genuinely exercises the collapsed-band path; max gap 0.000000). No band-collapse, no vacuous control, no alternate-optima flapping (per-day costs are deterministic on rerun). The weight mechanism is real: tilting changes the shared t=0 decision on 10-12 of 80 days. BUT the prior agent overstated three things. (1) WRONG SEM: driver line 211 computes the 'standard error' as np.std([sym_mean,t1_mean,t2_mean]) ~ 0.0007 AUD (reported '~0.006'), which is the spread of three near-equal aggregate means, NOT a sampling error. The TRUE day-level SEM of the mean is ~0.098 AUD. The headline 0.69% / 0.012 AUD mean 'improvement' is ~8x smaller than the real SEM and is statistically indistinguishable from zero -- it is NOT a demonstrated free lunch. (2) tilt1 != tilt2 EXACTLY: they differ on 2 of 80 days (max per-day gap 0.0026 AUD) and coincide only after rounding to 4 dp; the 'identical outcome / model artefact' framing is an overstatement of a rounding coincidence. (3) The -5.84% worst-case reduction rests on a SINGLE day (day 33), and tilting actually HURTS on 2 of the 10 changed days (days 15 and 62), so the worst-case benefit is fragile, not a robust hedge. None of these overturn the directional conclusions; they qualify the magnitude/precision claims.
final_takeaways: VERDICT: trustworthy. The experiment reproduces exactly (mean 1.7433 / P95 3.2067 / worst 3.7679 for sym; tilt1 and tilt2 both 1.7313 / 3.2067 / 3.5480 at 4 dp), the control is genuine and non-vacuous, and the LP is deterministic with no alternate-optima flapping. The headline conclusions are sound; only the magnitude/precision claims need correcting.

Tilting scenario weights toward the low-PV (P10) tail has ZERO effect on P95 (the 4th-worst-of-80 order statistic, 3.4537 AUD, lands on a day whose t=0 decision the weights do not change) and reduces the single worst day by ~5.8%. The P95 result is robust to weighting; the worst-case result rests on one day and is fragile.

The ~0.69% mean improvement is NOT a demonstrated effect: at 0.012 AUD it is roughly one-eighth of the true day-level SEM (~0.098 AUD), so it is statistically indistinguishable from zero. The prior 'free-lunch' framing should be dropped. (The driver's own SEM caveat is computed incorrectly -- it reports the spread of the three aggregate means, not a sampling error.)

tilt1 ([0.45,0.40,0.15]) and tilt2 ([0.60,0.30,0.10]) are NOT identical -- they diverge on 2 of 80 days (max 0.0026 AUD) and only round to the same 4-dp aggregates. The correct interpretation is that the marginal effect of further mass-shifting beyond tilt1 is negligible, not that the outcomes are exactly equal. The 8 kWh / 4 kW battery absorbs most of the conservatism via recourse, so the shared t=0 decision rarely moves.

Weight-tilting is NOT a substitute for CVaR here: it leaves P95 completely unmoved and its only visible effect (a handful of bad-PV days where the shared t=0 import/charge decision flips) cuts both ways -- it hurts cost on 2 of the 10 affected days. Symmetric weights [0.30,0.40,0.30] remain the recommended default; any tail benefit from tilting is within noise and not worth the complexity of justifying non-uniform scenario weights. For genuine quantile-risk control, use the explicit CVaR objective (cvar_blend experiment), not weight bias.

Caveats that stand: N=80, fixed seed 42; P95 is a single order statistic so the zero-delta could shift with more draws; aft_sd=0.3 drives unresolvable afternoon uncertainty; absolute AUD are stylised-model outputs (ratios/directions more reliable than magnitudes).
